explanation.text:
Maschil--literally, "giving instruction." The Psalmist describes the blessings of His forgiveness, succeeding the pains of conviction, and deduces from his own experience instruction and exhortation to others. (Psa 32:1-11)

(Compare Rom 4:6).

forgiven--literally, "taken away," opposed to retain (Joh 20:23).

covered--so that God no longer regards the sin (Psa 85:3).

bsb.title: Of David. A Maskil.
bsb.text: Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

explanation.text:
imputeth--charge to him, and treat him accordingly.

no guile--or, deceit, no false estimate of himself, nor insincerity before God (compare Rom 8:1).

bsb.text: Blessed is the man whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him, in whose spirit there is no deceit.

explanation.text:
A vivid description of felt, but unacknowledged, sin.

When--literally, "for," as in Psa 32:4.

bsb.text: When I kept silent, my bones became brittle from my groaning all day long.

explanation.text:
thy hand--of God, or power in distressing him (Psa 38:2).

moisture--vital juices of the body, the parching heat of which expresses the anguish of the soul. On the other figures, compare Psa 6:2, Psa 6:7; Psa 31:9-11. If composed on the occasion of the fifty-first Psalm, this distress may have been protracted for several months.

bsb.text: For day and night Your hand was heavy upon me; my strength was drained as in the summer heat. Selah

explanation.text: A prompt fulfilment of the purposed confession is followed by a prompt forgiveness.

bsb.text: Then I acknowledged my sin to You and did not hide my iniquity. I said, “I will confess my transgressions to the LORD,” and You forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah

explanation.text:
For this--that is, my happy experience.

godly--pious in the sense of Psa 4:3.

a time-- (Isa 55:6); when God's Spirit inclines us to seek pardon, He is ready to forgive.

floods, etc.--denotes great danger (Psa 18:17; Psa 66:12).

bsb.text: Therefore let all the godly pray to You while You may be found. Surely when great waters rise, they will not come near.

explanation.text: His experience illustrates the statement of Psa 32:6.

bsb.text: You are my hiding place. You protect me from trouble; You surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah

explanation.text:
Whether, as most likely, the language of David (compare Psa 51:13), or that of God, this is a promise of divine guidance.

I will . . . mine eye--or, My eye shall be on thee, watching and directing thy way.

bsb.text: I will instruct you and teach you the way you should go; I will give you counsel and watch over you.

explanation.text: The latter clause, more literally, "in that they come not near thee"; that is, because they will not come, etc., unless forced by bit and bridle.

bsb.text: Do not be like the horse or mule, which have no understanding; they must be controlled with bit and bridle to make them come to you.

explanation.text: The sorrows of the impenitent contrasted with the peace and safety secured by God's mercy.

bsb.text: Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but loving devotion surrounds him who trusts in the LORD.

explanation.text:
The righteous and upright, or those conforming to the divine teaching for securing the divine blessing, may well rejoice with shouting.

Next: Psalms Chapter 33

bsb.text: Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous ones; shout for joy, all you upright in heart.
